title: Hiring & Building an AI Engineering Team: Dr. Bryan Bischof
talk_summary: A hiring/team-building talk about how to staff AI product teams: which roles to hire in what order, what attributes predict impact (data intuition, product mindedness, urgency, curiosity), and how to interview for them.

takeaways.technique: Centralized AI platform team, not per-product integration
takeaways.what_they_do: One team owns the shared LLM provider integration, prompt infrastructure, and eval system; product teams consume it and each designate one person to interface with the platform team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every individual product team should not be going up and setting up their relationship with open AI separately

takeaways.what_they_do: Development order is: ship early product to users, then build evals, then gather feedback, then iterate; hiring is aligned to that order with a dedicated evaluation-quality role.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should start with an early product that you get in front of users then you should start by building evals

takeaways.technique: Small, high-signal challenge over LeetCode-style gates
takeaways.what_they_do: Replaces algorithmic puzzles with a scoped take-home that tests extracting meaning from messy data and scoping a minimum deliverable in a fixed time budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you were giving leak code interviews for your AI engineering hiring you are doing yourself a major disservice

takeaways.technique: Match staffing to development stage; avoid mythical man-month
takeaways.what_they_do: Hiring schedule mirrors the product development schedule; adding engineers to an early AI product does not compress timelines.
takeaways.evidence_quote: nine women cannot give birth in a single month

takeaways.technique: Work directly with domain experts / human-in-the-loop
takeaways.what_they_do: The AI capability is modeled on interactions with the people who actually do the job; experts use every build weekly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're building a customer support bot and you don't have customer support people using that every day you're insane
